findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded per request, so non-request code paths can miss English and default-locale strings
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` loads translations for the fallback chain, but it is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks and other code that calls `I18n.t` without going through a controller request never load the fallback locales. The patched `translate` in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, so when the requested locale lacks a key, the fallback lookup for `:en` or the site default hits an unloaded backend and returns a missing-translation string. The fallback behaviour is therefore request-dependent and inconsistent. Loading the fallback chain inside `translate` (or in the fallback lookup itself) would make it hold everywhere.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! runs on every request and allocates a new fallback array each time
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is executed on every request. Each call builds a fresh array via `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and iterates it, calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each entry. It reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` each time. This is cheap but unnecessary per-request work that could be memoised or moved to a single load step.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! reads and lazily initialises @loaded_locales outside the mutex
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` performs `@loaded_locales ||= []` and an unsynchronised `include?` check before calling `load_locale`. Two threads can race on the lazy initialisation, and the first check reads the shared array without the LOAD_MUTEX that protects writes. `load_locale` re-checks inside the mutex so the final result is correct, but the unlocked read and the `||=` initialisation are inconsistent with the locking discipline used elsewhere in the same file.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList overrides only [] on a Hash, so other Hash accessors return inconsistent results
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `[]` to compute a computed fallback chain, but the underlying hash is never populated. Methods such as `fetch`, `key?`, `has_key?` or `dig` still use the empty stored data, so they disagree with `[]`. Any caller that uses these methods, including I18n internals that may check membership, gets different answers. A plain object with a single `[]` method would be clearer and safer.
